hook.situation: You just finished watching a Korean film with a friend. She asks '이 영화 어땠어요?' You want to say it was a bit slow — but you don't want to sound too blunt. You try '좀 느려요' and it sounds like you're stating a fact. Your friend raises an eyebrow. In Korean, the difference between 'it IS slow' and 'it SEEMS slow' is one short grammar ending — and natives use the softer version almost every time.
objectives: Use -는 것 같다 to express soft opinions and guesses without sounding arrogant
Use -잖아(요) to remind someone of something you both already know
Use -거든(요) to introduce new background information as a reason or explanation
hook.whyItMatters: At B1 level, the gap between textbook Korean and real conversation is mostly about hedging. Koreans rarely state opinions as bare facts — they soften them with -것 같다, link them to shared knowledge with -잖아, or introduce reasons with -거든. Learn these three endings and you'll immediately sound less like a robot and more like someone who understands Korean social nuance.

grammarNotes.title: -는 것 같다 — soft opinions and impressions
grammarNotes.func: Use -는 것 같다 to say 'it seems / I think / probably' instead of stating something as a flat fact. It softens your opinion so you sound less blunt and more polite, even when you're fairly sure.

formTable.ex: 오다 → 오는 것 같다 (seems to be coming); 먹다 → 먹는 것 같다
비싸다 → 비싼 것 같다 (seems expensive); 크다 → 큰 것 같다
작다 → 작은 것 같다 (seems small); 좋다 → 좋은 것 같다
가다 → 간 것 같다 (seems to have gone); 먹다 → 먹은 것 같다
오다 → 올 것 같다 (will probably come); 없다 → 없을 것 같다
학생 → 학생인 것 같다 (seems to be a student)

examples.ko: 지금 밖에 비가 오는 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: jigeum bakke biga oneun geot gatayo.
examples.en: It seems to be raining outside right now.
examples.note: Action verb, present: 오는 것 같다, because the rain is happening now.

examples.ko: 이 책은 좀 어려운 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: i chaegeun jom eoryeoun geot gatayo.
examples.en: This book seems a bit hard.
examples.note: Adjective 어렵다 (받침, ㅂ-irregular) → 어려운 것 같다; softer than just 어려워요.

examples.ko: 친구가 벌써 집에 간 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: chinguga beolsseo jibe gan geot gatayo.
examples.en: It seems my friend already went home.
examples.note: Past guess: 가다 → 간 것 같다 for something that already happened.

examples.en: I probably won't have time tomorrow.
examples.note: Future/guess: 없다 → 없을 것 같다; a gentle, indirect way to say no.

keyPoint.label: present 는 것 같다 vs future 을 것 같다
keyPoint.body: Use -는 것 같다 for something you can sense right now (비가 오는 것 같아요 — I can hear/see it). Use -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 for a guess about the future or when you have no direct evidence yet (비가 올 것 같아요 — the sky looks like it). For the past, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 (간 것 같아요). Don't worry about every irregular form yet — just get the present/past/future split right.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 것 같다 sounds like [걷 깓따]: 것 ends in a [t], which tenses the next ㄱ so 같 comes out as [깓]. In casual speech it often blurs to [거 같아요].

drill.instruction: Soften each blunt statement into a -는 것 같다 impression. Watch the tense.
drill.model: 이 영화 재미있어요. → 이 영화 재미있는 것 같아요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 나는 이 책이 어려운 것 같다고 생각해요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers tack a separate '나는 ~ 생각해요' (I think) onto -는 것 같다, but -는 것 같다 already means 'I think / it seems,' so you'd be saying it twice. Also, 것 같다 changes with tense (present 어려운, past 어려웠던, future 어려울) — English 'seems' stays the same, Korean doesn't.

grammarNotes.title: -잖아(요) vs -거든(요) — shared info vs new info
grammarNotes.func: Both end a sentence to give a reason or background, but they point in opposite directions. -잖아(요) reminds the listener of something you BOTH already know ('you know...', 'remember?'). -거든(요) gives information that's NEW to the listener, often the reason behind what you just said.

formTable.ex: 있다 → 있잖아요; 바쁘다 → 바쁘잖아요 (you know I'm busy)
가다 → 갔잖아요 (we did go, remember); 먹다 → 먹었잖아요
바쁘다 → 바쁘거든요 (the thing is, I'm busy); 좋다 → 좋거든요
가다 → 갔거든요 (the thing is, I went); 먹다 → 먹었거든요

examples.en: Let's hurry. We don't have time, you know.
examples.note: -잖아요: the listener already knows time is short; you're reminding them.

examples.ko: 어제 그 영화 같이 봤잖아요. 진짜 재미있었어요.
examples.romanization: eoje geu yeonghwa gachi bwatjanayo. jinjja jaemiisseosseoyo.
examples.en: We watched that movie together yesterday, remember? It was really fun.

examples.ko: A: 왜 안 와요? B: 지금 일이 많거든요.
examples.romanization: A: wae an wayo? B: jigeum iri mankeodeunyo.
examples.en: A: Why aren't you coming? B: The thing is, I've got a lot of work right now.
examples.note: -거든요: B's workload is NEW info that answers A's question.

examples.ko: 요즘 한국어를 공부해요. 다음 달에 한국에 가거든요.
examples.romanization: yojeum hangugeoreul gongbuhaeyo. daeum dare hanguge gageodeunyo.
examples.en: I'm studying Korean these days. It's because I'm going to Korea next month.
examples.note: -거든요 gives the new reason behind the first sentence.

keyPoint.label: -잖아요 (you know) vs -거든요 (the thing is)
keyPoint.body: Ask yourself: does the listener already know this? If YES, use -잖아요 ('you know...', 'remember?'). If NO and you're telling them for the first time, use -거든요 ('the thing is...', 'because...'). Using -잖아요 for brand-new info can sound like you're scolding them for not already knowing.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: -잖아요 is pronounced [자나요]: 잖 has a silent ㅎ in its 받침, so it just links smoothly into 아요. -거든요 is simply [거든뇨], with the final 요 tucked on — no special change.

drill.instruction: Choose -잖아요 (shared knowledge) or -거든요 (new info) and finish the sentence.
drill.model: (reminding a friend you both know it's closed today) 오늘 문 닫았잖아요.
items: (reminding: we both know she's busy) 민수 씨한테 부탁하지 마세요. 그 사람 요즘 ____ .
(new reason why you can't eat it) 저는 그거 안 먹어요. 제가 채식주의자____ .
(reminding: we already paid) 또 돈 내요? 우리 아까 ____ .

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 저 지금 못 가요. 일이 많잖아요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 저 지금 못 가요. 일이 많거든요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English uses one phrase, 'because / you see,' for both situations, so learners reach for -잖아요 every time. But if the listener doesn't already know your reason, -잖아요 wrongly implies 'as you obviously know,' which sounds blaming. For information you're sharing for the first time, you need -거든요.

exampleSentence.ko: 제 생각에는 이 방법이 더 좋을 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: In my opinion, I think this method is better.
exampleSentence.note: 제 생각에는 = 'in my view' — a standard phrase for introducing soft opinions in conversation
More formal than 생각 — used in meetings, discussions, and written Korean

exampleSentence.en: There's a reason, you see. Let me explain.
exampleSentence.note: -거든요 introduces the fact of having a reason as new information, then promises the full explanation

exampleSentence.ko: 그 강의 진짜 지루한 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.note: Adjective → -(으)ㄴ 것 같다: 지루한 것 같다. Bare 지루해요 would sound like a harsh verdict

exampleSentence.en: I found it fun, actually. I rather liked it.
exampleSentence.note: -거든요: introducing a contrasting opinion the other person didn't know you held — new information to explain your reaction

exampleSentence.ko: 이 소설은 전개가 느린 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: I think this novel's pacing is slow.
exampleSentence.note: 느리다 is an adjective → 느린 것 같다. 전개 is commonly used in film and book reviews

exampleSentence.en: I think the ending was a bit disappointing.
exampleSentence.note: 아쉽다 (to feel a lack, to be slightly disappointing) → 아쉬운 것 같다. Softening a criticism with -것 같다 is natural here

exampleSentence.ko: 그 배우 연기 정말 잘하거든요. 꼭 봐 보세요.
exampleSentence.en: That actor is genuinely great at acting, you see. Definitely watch it.
exampleSentence.note: -거든요 here shares a personal assessment as new information, then follows up with a recommendation
자연스럽다 (to be natural) → irregular: 자연스러운 것 같다. The ㅂ irregular applies here

extendedVocabulary.english: to feel a slight lack, to be a (gentle) disappointment

exampleSentence.en: I think the end was a bit unsatisfying.
exampleSentence.note: ㅂ irregular adjective: 아쉽다 → 아쉬운 것 같다. This exact phrase is very common in Korean reviews and casual talk

exampleSentence.en: The protagonist seems a bit too perfect.
exampleSentence.note: 완벽하다 (to be perfect) → 완벽한 것 같다. Common critique in drama reviews

exampleSentence.ko: 그 인물한테 공감하기 어려운 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: I think it's hard to relate to that character.
exampleSentence.note: 공감하기 어렵다 = 'it's hard to empathize' — the -기 turns 공감하다 into a noun, then 어렵다 (hard) applies → 어려운 것 같다

exampleSentence.ko: 개인적으로는 이 영화가 좀 과대평가된 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: Personally, I think this movie is a bit overrated.
exampleSentence.note: 개인적으로 + -것 같다 is a double-hedging strategy very common in Korean — softens with both 'personally' and 'seems'

exampleSentence.en: To be honest, I was a bit disappointed, you see.
exampleSentence.note: -거든요 after an honest admission: the speaker is sharing the real reason/feeling the listener may not have guessed

exampleSentence.en: It seems everyone evaluates it differently.
exampleSentence.note: Verb → -는 것 같다: 평가하는 것 같다. Using this form for a general observation about people in general is very natural

extendedVocabulary.english: to expect, to look forward to

exampleSentence.en: I had high expectations, so I was a bit let down, you see.
exampleSentence.note: -거든요 again here: explaining personal background (had expectations) that the listener didn't know — this is why the disappointment makes sense

exampleSentence.ko: 이 드라마 추천할 만한 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: I think this drama is worth recommending.
exampleSentence.note: 추천할 만하다 = 'worth recommending' → 추천할 만한 것 같다. The -(으)ㄹ 만한 것 같다 construction softens a recommendation

extendedDialogue.setting: Minjun and Yujin are having coffee after watching a film at the cinema. They're comparing their reactions.

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 유진 씨, 영화 어땠어요? 저는 좀 아쉬웠어요. 기대가 컸거든요.
lines.romanization: Yujin ssi, yeonghwa eottaesseoyo? Jeoneun jom aswiwosseoyo. Gidaega keotgeodeunyo.
lines.en: Yujin, how was the movie? I was a bit disappointed. My expectations were high, you see.
lines.grammarNote: -거든요: Minjun gives the background reason for his disappointment. 기대가 컸거든요 explains why 아쉬웠어요 makes sense.

lines.speaker: 유진
lines.ko: 그래요? 저는 꽤 재미있었는데요. 전개가 좀 느린 것 같긴 했지만.
lines.romanization: Geuraeyo? Jeoneun kkwae jaemiisseonneundeyo. Jeongaega jom neurin geot gatgin haetjiman.
lines.en: Really? I found it quite fun. Though I did think the pacing was a bit slow.
lines.grammarNote: -는 것 같긴 했지만: conceding a partial criticism (slow pacing) using -것 같다 in the past; 긴 했지만 = 'though it did seem that way'

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 맞아요! 전개가 너무 느리잖아요. 2시간 동안 뭔가 일어나는 게 별로 없었어요.
lines.romanization: Majayo! Jeongaega neomu neurijanayo. Du-sigan dongan mwonga ireonaneun ge byeollo eopseosseoyo.
lines.en: Right! The pacing really is too slow, you know. Not much happens in those two hours.
lines.grammarNote: -잖아요: both viewers just experienced the film, so the slow pacing is shared observable knowledge — Minjun is nudging Yujin to agree

lines.speaker: 유진
lines.ko: 음, 그래도 배우들 연기가 굉장히 좋은 것 같았어요.
lines.romanization: Eum, geuraedo baeudeul yeongiga goengjanghi joeun geot gatassoyo.
lines.en: Hmm, but I thought the acting was really good though.
lines.grammarNote: -것 같았어요: past tense of -것 같다, expressing a personal impression during and after watching

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 그건 저도 동의해요. 특히 주인공 배우가 정말 잘하거든요.
lines.romanization: Geugeon jeodo donguihaeyo. Teuki juingong baeuga jeongmal jalhageodeunyo.
lines.en: I agree on that. Especially the lead actor — they're genuinely great, you see.
lines.grammarNote: -거든요: Minjun adds this as a reason or supporting fact the listener may not have fully appreciated yet

lines.speaker: 유진
lines.ko: 맞아요, 연기가 자연스러운 것 같아요. 억지스럽지 않잖아요.
lines.romanization: Majayo, yeongiga jayeonseureoun geot gatayo. Eokjiseureopji anjanayo.
lines.en: Exactly, the acting seems natural. It's not forced, you know.
lines.grammarNote: Two different endings: 자연스러운 것 같아요 (soft impression) + 억지스럽지 않잖아요 (shared observable fact — both can see it's not forced)

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 그래서 결말이 좀 더 강했으면 좋았을 것 같아요. 솔직히 좀 아쉬웠거든요.
lines.romanization: Geuraeseo gyeolmari jom deo ganghaesseumyeon joasseul geot gatayo. Soljiki jom aswieotgeodeunyo.
lines.en: That's why I think it would've been better if the ending were stronger. Honestly, I was a bit disappointed, you see.
lines.grammarNote: -것 같아요 on a conditional (강했으면 좋았을 것 같다) softens what would otherwise sound like demanding criticism; -거든요 introduces the honest emotional reaction

lines.speaker: 유진
lines.ko: 개인적으로는 이런 열린 결말을 좋아하거든요. 생각할 거리가 많잖아요.
lines.romanization: Gaeinjeogeuro-neun ireon yeollin gyeolmareul joahageodeunyo. Saenggakhal georiga manchanayo.
lines.en: Personally, I like open endings like this, you see. There's a lot to think about, you know.
lines.grammarNote: 개인적으로는 + -거든요 = double personal-framing; then -잖아요 to invite agreement on the 'lots to think about' observation

readingText.title: 영화 보고 나서 (After the Movie)
readingText.body:
유진: 민준 씨, 아까 그 영화 어땠어요? 저는 꽤 좋았거든요.
민준: 저는 좀 아쉬웠어요. 기대가 너무 컸던 것 같아요.
유진: 아, 그래요? 전 결말이 인상적인 것 같았는데.
민준: 저는 결말이 좀 급한 것 같았어요. 그리고 스토리가 단순한 것 같기도 하고요.
유진: 음... 그래도 배우들 연기만큼은 정말 좋았잖아요.
민준: 그건 맞아요. 특히 주인공 배우가 굉장한 것 같아요. 이제 팬이 됐거든요!
유진: 저도요! 다음에 그 배우 나오는 드라마 같이 봐요.
readingText.bodyTranslation:
Yujin: Minjun, how was that movie earlier? I quite liked it, you see.
Minjun: I was a bit disappointed. I think my expectations were too high.
Yujin: Oh, really? I thought the ending was impressive.
Minjun: I thought the ending felt a bit rushed. And I thought the story was kind of simple too.
Yujin: Hmm... But the acting was really good, you know.
Minjun: That's true. Especially the lead actor seems amazing. I've become a fan, you see!
Yujin: Me too! Next time let's watch the drama that actor's in together.

comprehensionQuestions.question: How does Minjun feel about the movie overall? What specific issues does he mention?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: Minjun was disappointed (아쉬웠어요). He thought his expectations were too high (기대가 너무 컸던 것 같아요), the ending felt rushed (결말이 좀 급한 것 같았어요), and the story was a bit simple (스토리가 단순한 것 같기도 하고요).

comprehensionQuestions.question: What do both Minjun and Yujin agree on?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: They both agree the acting was great, especially the lead actor (배우들 연기만큼은 정말 좋았잖아요 / 주인공 배우가 굉장한 것 같아요). They both became fans of the actor (저도요!).

comprehensionQuestions.question: Find every -것 같다, -잖아요, and -거든요 in the text. For each one, explain why that ending was chosen and not one of the other two.
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 1) 기대가 너무 컸던 것 같아요 — Minjun uses -것 같다 (past: -던 것 같다) to frame his high expectations as a personal impression/self-reflection, softening self-criticism. 2) 결말이 인상적인 것 같았는데 — Yujin hedges her positive reaction as a personal impression (past -것 같다), not a fact. 3) 결말이 좀 급한 것 같았어요 and 스토리가 단순한 것 같기도 하고요 — Minjun consistently uses -것 같다 to soften criticisms into impressions. 4) 배우들 연기만큼은 정말 좋았잖아요 — -잖아요 fits here because both speakers JUST WATCHED the film together — the good acting is shared, observable knowledge Yujin is reminding Minjun of. 5) 좋았거든요 (Yujin's opening) — -거든요 because Yujin is volunteering her positive reaction as NEW personal information Minjun didn't know yet. 6) 이제 팬이 됐거든요 — -거든요 because Minjun is sharing a new personal fact (becoming a fan) that Yujin didn't know.

culturalNote.title: 왜 한국인은 항상 '것 같아요'를 쓸까요? — Why Koreans always say 'it seems'
culturalNote.body: If you watch any Korean variety show or drama, you'll notice that Koreans rarely state opinions as flat facts — they're constantly hedging with -것 같아요, -것 같은데요, -것 같긴 해요. This isn't uncertainty or lack of confidence; it's a deep cultural preference for avoiding confrontational directness. Saying '이 영화 별로예요' (This movie isn't great) can come across as dismissive and final — it invites no discussion. But '이 영화가 별로인 것 같아요' opens space for the other person to disagree gracefully. This extends to professional settings too: in meetings, Koreans often frame even strong opinions as -것 같습니다 to maintain group harmony (눈치 culture). Mastering -것 같다 isn't just grammar — it's learning to speak with appropriate Korean social grace.

inlineExercises.prompt: 이 음식이 좀 짠___ 것 같아요. (I think this food is a bit salty.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 짜다 is an adjective with a vowel-ending stem (짜-), so the modifier is ㄴ: 짠 것 같아요. 는 is for present verb modifiers, and 은 is used after consonant-ending adjective stems.

inlineExercises.prompt: 저 오늘 못 가요. 약속이 있___. (I can't go today. I have plans.)
inlineExercises.explanation: -거든요 is correct because the speaker is giving the listener NEW information (the plans) as a reason. -잖아요 would only work if the listener already knew about the plans. '-는 것 같아요' expresses uncertainty — but the speaker KNOWS they have plans, so that would be odd.

inlineExercises.prompt: 다음 문장에서 틀린 것을 찾아보세요: '그 배우 유명하는 것 같아요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 유명하다 is an adjective (not a verb), so it takes the adjective modifier -ㄴ/-은, not the verb modifier -는. 유명하다 has a vowel-ending stem (유명하-), so the modifier is -ㄴ → 유명한 것 같아요. This is the most common -것 같다 mistake among English learners.

inlineExercises.prompt: Your friend says '나 왜 화났는지 알아?' You reply: '어제 네가 약속을 안 지켰___ .' Which ending fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: -잖아 is correct here. The person you're talking TO is the one who broke the promise — they KNOW they did it. You're reminding them of their own action as the reason for your anger. -거든 would mean 'just so you know you broke the promise' — but they clearly already know. -는 것 같아 would express uncertainty about whether they broke it, which is too weak for this situation.

inlineExercises.prompt: Translate: 'I think it's going to rain tomorrow.'
inlineExercises.hint: Decide whether the rain is happening now, already happened, or expected later. Then choose the modifier before 것 같아요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 비가 올 것 같아요 is a softened future guess, not a firm plan. The future modifier 올 fits because the rain is expected tomorrow.

inlineExercises.prompt: At work, a colleague offers to switch to English because you look unsure. You want to say you can keep using Korean because you're actually quite good at it. Which is correct?
options: 사실 저 한국어 꽤 잘하는 것 같아요.
inlineExercises.explanation: -거든요 is correct because you're giving NEW background information as a reason to continue in Korean. -잖아요 would imply they already knew you were good at Korean. -는 것 같아요 would sound strangely uncertain — 'I seem to be good at Korean?' That doesn't convey confidence; it sounds like you're guessing about your own skill.

inlineExercises.prompt: 그 식당 오늘 문 닫___ 것 같아요. 불이 꺼져 있어요. (That restaurant seems to be closed today. The lights are off.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 닫다 (to close/be closed) is a verb, but here we're inferring a PRESENT STATE from evidence — the speaker means 'it seems closed right now.' The present state is expressed with the adjective-like -(으)ㄴ modifier: 닫은 것 같다 (seems closed). If you used 닫는 것 같다 it would mean 'seems to be in the process of closing,' and 닫을 것 같다 would mean 'seems like it will close (in the future).' The correct reading is current state: 닫은 것 같다.

inlineExercises.prompt: 약속___ 있거든요. (I have plans, you see.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 있거든요 still uses 이/가 for the thing that exists or is possessed. 을 would wrongly treat 약속 as an object of an action.
Adjectives use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 for a softened impression. 지루하다 becomes 지루한 것 같아요, not 지루하는 것 같아요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'I think this movie is a little boring.'
inlineExercises.correct: 이 영화는 좀 지루한 것 같아요
inlineExercises.explanation: 좀 softens the criticism, and -한 것 같아요 makes it an impression rather than a blunt fact. This is much safer than saying 이 영화는 지루해요 directly.

bullets: -는 것 같다 = FROSTED GLASS: softens opinions/guesses into impressions; verbs use -는, adjectives use -(으)ㄴ, past uses -(으)ㄴ, future uses -(으)ㄹ
-잖아(요) = REPLAY BUTTON: reminds listener of something they already know or should know — shared information
-거든(요) = UPLOAD BUTTON: introduces new background information or a reason the listener didn't have — use this when telling someone something for the first time

writingTask.prompt: Write a short comment giving your opinion about a movie you just watched, softening it and adding a reason.
writingTask.hint: Use -는 것 같다 to soften your opinion, and use -거든요 (new info) or -잖아요 (shared info) to give a reason.
writingTask.model: 이 영화는 좀 지루한 것 같아요. 전개가 너무 느리거든요. 그래도 배우 연기는 좋잖아요.
writingTask.modelEn: I think this movie is a bit boring. The pacing is too slow (you see). But the acting is good, you know.

canDo: Soften an opinion so it sounds less blunt (-는 것 같다)
Give a reason as new information the listener didn't know (-거든요)
Remind the listener of something you both already know (-잖아요)
Talk about a movie or story using 전개 · 결말 · 연기 · 주인공
